newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump on privatisation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump on privatisation hopes.

text.p: Turkish stocks jumped an average 3.19 percent on Monday in selective trade led by largely state owned shares due to market-moving remarks by the country's new privatisation chief, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 which brushed a high of 2,039 in the afternoon session, ended 63 points, or 3.19 percent, higher at 2,036. This compared to an all-time high close of 2,043 on July 14.
Daily trade volume jumped 10.2 percent to 29.36 trillion lira from Friday's 26.64 trillion.
Several brokers said the turnover was not strong enough to support the increase in the market index.

"Trade volume did not confirm the rise and most of it came from the deals in state shares. Technically, the index's next resistance will be at 2,000-2,065 range," Ersel Alkay from Marbas Securities said.

The rally in state shares was led by flat steel giant Eregli which alone made up 10.3 percent of the total volume. Turnover in five bluechip state enterprises totalled 6.22 trillion lira, or 21.2 percent of total.
Brokers said remarks by Yalcin Atli, the newly appointed acting chairman of the privatisation administration (OIB) boosted buying in state shares in the afternoon.

Atli said the country's sell-off programme would be revitalised after faltering during the change of government. "There has been a delay of one month. We will continue our work at speed to make up for this delay," he told Reuters.

Brokers said inflation figures released earlier in the day did not undermine sentiment. Wholesale prices rose 5.3 percent and consumer prices climed 6.3 percent month-on-month in July, compared to rises of 3.4 percent and 2.9 percent in June.

First half budget results announced in the afternoon were also disregarded by the market players. The budget deficit at end-June stood at 681.7 trillion lira, up sharply from 475.4 trillion a year ago, the Treasury said.

The most heavily traded stocks of the day were Eregli, up 2,500 lira at 28,000, largely state-owned petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi, up 3,000 lira at 32,000 and T.Is Bank's C series, up 4,000 to 59,000 lira.

Of the 250 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 132 to 63 and 55 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial rose 2.94 percent to 1,960, the IMKB Services inched up 0.62 percent to 1,944 and the IMKB Financial leapt 3.58 percent to 2,199.
The highest increase was seen in the index representing the metals sector with a 7.29 percent gain.

The Exchange said it would list partial shares of leading Turkish tractor producer Uzel Makina Sanayii AS on the national market on Tuesday at an opening price of 19,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal valued share.
The company had last week floated 345 billion lira or 15 percent of its capital in a two-day public offer whose 85 percent was sold to institutional investors abroad.
